title: Smart snap and scroll-handoff for console panels, charts, and modal stacks
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Reduce layout jank and cross-browser regressions across the Redwood Console's heavy surfaces: dashboard panels, data tables with virtualization, interactive charts (canvas/SVG), and nested modal stacks. Deliver a small set of production-ready CSS rules, JS handoff logic for scroll/snap, and a prototype that demonstrates modal stacking, focus preservation, and chart reflow under window/resolution changes.
engineering_notes: Primary implementation options discussed: CSS position:sticky + intersectionObserver vs JS-based scroll-handoff using requestAnimationFrame. Eng prefers minimal JS: sticky for anchored panels, polyfill for Safari where sticky inside transformed parents fails.
Virtualized tables: need to avoid layout thrash on resize. Proposed: debounce container width measurement, expose a stable column-width token from CSS for renderer to read before reflow.
Chart canvas scaling: prefer devicePixelRatio-aware redraw on resize and a fallback low-res raster for iOS 15 older Safari to avoid 60fps frame drops.
Modal stacking: resolved z-index layering and backdrop pointer-events; added focus-trap rules and aria-hidden toggling for underlying content.
Performance target: first meaningful paint of dashboard rearrange should be < 120ms on mid-range laptop; continuous reflow on resize should be visually smooth under 16ms frame target where possible.
qa_notes: Cross-browser checklist added: Chromium desktop (latest), Firefox desktop (latest), Safari macOS (Big Sur+), Safari iOS (14+), Edge (Chromium), and Android WebView.
Known issues: Safari iOS double-scroll on nested overflow containers — workaround included in prototype using touch-action manipulation and pointer-events gating.
Suggested automated visual tests: Percy snapshots at multiple widths (320, 375, 768, 1024, 1440) and high-DPI variants.
Accessibility QA: keyboard traversal through modal stacks, logical tab order, and focus return verified in prototype; documented exceptions for legacy Safari focus quirks.
accessibility_notes: Ensure all sticky/anchored panels do not trap keyboard focus. Add skip-links for screen reader users to bypass dense interactive areas like charts and tables.

Modal stacking: use aria-modal and aria-hidden on background siblings; ensure screen readers announce modal title on open. For nested modals, announce stacking level and provide clear cancel/close affordances.
Color contrast checks for newly surfaced control outlines in compact mode added to spec.

2026-03-05 QA: 'Observed a 200ms reflow spike on Firefox when toggling density mode with many table rows. Recommend measuring paint timing and deferring heavy recalculation.'
2026-03-09 Accessibility review (Ava Martinez): 'Keyboard flow works but VoiceOver on Safari reports unexpected live-region updates; isolate live-region mutations to avoid spurious announcements.'
decisions: Use CSS position:sticky for anchored headers/side panels as default; add small JS fallback that reclassifies elements when sticky fails in a given browser.
Adopt a stable API for renderer to read CSS tokens for column widths to avoid layout flip when toggling density or resizing panels.
Implement modal stacking conventions: a single backdrop layer, increasing z-index per modal, aria-hidden applied to non-active modal siblings, and a documented focus-return behavior.
Provide chart redraw debounce of 100ms on rapid resize events and immediate redraw on pointer-driven manual resizing to keep UX snappy without thrashing.
Rollout strategy: feature-flagged visual changes, opt-in for Dedicated customers via console flags for initial telemetry gathering.
